description: Kung Pao Chicken is a vibrant, spicy, and savory Sichuan classic featuring tender chicken, crunchy peanuts, and a delightful kick from dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns. This iconic dish balances sweet, sour, and fiery notes, creating an unforgettable culinary experience that truly awakens the palate. It is a beloved staple in Chinese cuisine, perfect for a satisfying lunch or dinner.

white parts sliced, green parts chopped

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a medium bowl, combine the cubed chicken with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, 1 tbsp cornstarch, and 1 tsp sesame oil. Mix well until the chicken is evenly coated. Let it marinate for at least 15 minutes at room temperature, or up to 30 minutes in the refrigerator.

instructions.title: Prepare the Kung Pao Sauce
instructions.text: In a small bowl, whisk together the 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp dark soy sauce (if using), 1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, 1 tbsp Chinkiang vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp cornstarch, and 2 tbsp chicken broth or water. Stir until the sugar and cornstarch are fully dissolved. Set aside.

instructions.title: Sear the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of cooking oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until shimmering. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until lightly browned and mostly cooked through. Remove the chicken from the wok and set aside.

instructions.title: Infuse the Oil
instructions.text: Add the remaining 1 tablespoon of cooking oil to the wok. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add the dried red chilies and Sichuan peppercorns. Stir-fry for about 30-60 seconds until fragrant and the chilies darken slightly. Be careful not to burn them.

instructions.title: Add Aromatics and Chicken
instructions.text: Quickly add the minced ginger, minced garlic, and the white parts of the sliced green onions to the wok. Stir-fry for another 30 seconds until fragrant. Return the seared chicken to the wok.

instructions.title: Combine with Sauce and Peanuts
instructions.text: Give the prepared Kung Pao sauce a quick stir, then pour it over the chicken and aromatics in the wok. Increase the heat to high and stir-fry continuously for 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken evenly. Stir in the roasted peanuts and the chopped green parts of the green onions.

instructions.title: Serve Immediately
instructions.text: Remove from heat and, if desired, drizzle with 1/2 tsp Sichuan peppercorn oil for an extra layer of numbing spice. Serve your authentic Kung Pao Chicken hot, ideally with steamed white rice.

tips: Use a very hot wok or large skillet to stir-fry the chicken quickly, which helps achieve a tender texture and prevents it from steaming.
For an authentic 'ma la' (numbing and spicy) flavor, do not skip the Sichuan peppercorns. Toast them lightly before adding to the oil for maximum aroma.
Best served immediately with steamed jasmine rice. Leftovers can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days; reheat gently to maintain texture.
